[title26][sentence]
This looks like a security station.  There are
a couple monitors on a desk with some
controls on them.

[title29][sentence]
This is the security station.  It was
from here that you turned
off all the force fields.

[title25][sentence]
You give the grate a couple kicks
and nothing happens.  You work up
a bit of adrenaline and try again.  This
time you hear a loud snap as the latch
gives way.

[title30][sentence]
You trashed the latch when
you first kicked this grate open,
so now all it needs is a gentle
little push . . . .

[title27][sentence]
Other than an expired insurance card
and a couple of wadded up tissues,
there doesn't seem to be anything of
interest in the glove compartment.

[title27][sentence]
You recognize the controls here as
the type manufacturers are legally
required to install, even though the
vehicle is fully automated.  They
look like they would be barely 
adequate in the event the automatic
system failed.

[title26][sentence]
What a mess.  Whoever owned this car
was a serious slob.  Apart from the ubiquitous
stuffed cat on the windshield, there is a pile of
soda cans on the floor and a layer of grime on all the
controls.  The central control screen has a thick
layer of dust on it.
[title27][sentence]\nThis deodorizer ran out of 'pleasant-smelling\nevergreen disinfectant' about a hundred years ago.

[title26][sentence]
Before you say anything nasty about the
person who left these here, think about
the conditions inside of your refrigerator.
[title20][sentence]\nHA! Got one!  Oh.  Wait.  It's only\nsuction cupped there.  Drat!
[title26][sentence]\nThrough the amber windshield you can\nsee part of the city, and all of a stuffed cat.

[title30][sentence]
Since there is no rear windshield on this
car you assume this must actually be
a video display.  The rear-view camera
appears to be dead.
[title25][sentence]\nIt's mounted too well to be plucked off.
[title25][sentence]\nIt is disgusting and smelly.  In a way\nit makes you feel right at home.

[title30][sentence]
No.  Believe it or not this actually
smells worse than your own.  You would
do better just to keep yours until you
find some clean socks to change into.

[title32][sentence]
You fiddle with the car controls, but
nothing seems to work.  Apparently, that
little scanner doesn't like what it sees.
[title27][sentence]\nThe scanner consists of a large square plate\nwith a hand-shaped depression in it.

[title29][sentence]
The monitor is no longer operational.  It
appears that a kidney struck the front of the
picture tube with enough impact energy
to completely destroy the monitor.

[title30][sentence]
The monitor is no longer operational.  It
appears that a rock struck the front of the
picture tube with enough impact energy
to completely destroy the monitor.
[title22][sentence]\nThis display's information is probably\nuseful to someone.  But not to you.

[title20][sentence]
Whoever modeled for this statue was
obviously a beautiful woman.  You decide
to consider a career in sculpting if you
ever get off this planet.

[title27][sentence]
This must have belonged to that dead
guard over there.  You find it odd that
there is no tape in it.
[title26][sentence]\nIt's wrecked--like most things in this room.

[title26][sentence]
Yech!  An amputated arm lies on the
floor.  The hand is empty, and the elbow
is bent slightly.
[title25][sentence]\nYou ponder the possible uses of such a device.\nAfter a moment you give up.
[title25][sentence]\nIt's about time for you to find\nthat vase and get off this planet.
[title27][sentence]\nYou haven't a clue what this gauge\nmeasures.
[title21][sentence]\nThis where that guard put all your stuff\nwhen you were captured.

[title25][sentence]
Good news!  Most of your belongings are
still here.  What's missing has probably
been taken away for analysis.

[title26][sentence]
Wouldn't you know it: nothing but worthless
junk.  It looks like they are long overdue for
garage sale.

[title27][sentence]
You remember begin led down
this hall when you were captured.
The hall is now in pretty sad shape.

[title25][sentence]
This is the security room where you
had that stimulating pat down.  Since 
then things have changed for the worse.
Most of the equipment is destroyed and
there is a dead guard lying on the floor.
[title22][sentence]\nYou don't need any of these things.
[title25][sentence]\nGood idea.  You never know when you'll\nget the urge to crank up some tunes.

[title26][sentence]
You carefully pick up the amputated
arm.  You decide to carry it around
for as short a period of time as possible.

[title25][sentence]
The desk is broken in about a thousand
places.  The extent of the damage in
this room amazes you.

[title32][sentence]
Look at that!  It's the same woman who
patted you down and took away all
your stuff.  It doesn't look like she's 
going to be giving you any more pat-downs
now.  Too bad.  She appears to be missing
an arm and one or more internal organs.

[title27][sentence]
There is another room through this
doorway.  It looks like it has had the
same kind of rough day this room has
had.
[title18][sentence]\nThe table has been splintered.

[title29][sentence]
The projector has been damaged
beyond repair.  Your friend didn't
miss much coming through here.

[title30][sentence]
It's a good thing your massive friend
didn't take this support out.  The whole
room probably would have caved in.
At least he showed some restraint.
[title16][sentence]\nIt's completely destroyed.\n

[title30][sentence]
The view screen is to be divided into
three main regions.  The first describes
your currently selected destination; the
second shows you a schematic map of
the city; and the third relays some system
status information in characters that are
meaningless to you.

[title24][sentence]
The control panel consists of a view screen,
some kind of indicator (which appears broken),
and some buttons.

[title30][sentence]
The street continues deep into the heart of the
city.  You can't help but notice what has got to
be the gaudiest condominium you have ever seen.
A large sign announces the residence of someone
who must have a serious neon fetish.

[title30][sentence]
The street continues deep into the heart of the
city.  You can't help but notice what has got to
be the gaudiest condominium you have ever seen.
A large sign announces the residence of someone
who must have a serious neon fetish.  You notice
a pencil thin beam of light protruding from the
roof.

[title26][sentence]
This is the car you arrived in.  It has
not changed significantly since you
left it.

[title26][sentence]
The large coliseum in the distance
occupies several city blocks.  It is
almost as big as the sports arena you
frequent on Umbilica IV.
[title24][sentence]\nThe buildings here do not interest you.

[title20][sentence]
Exploring this entire city on
foot would be a bad plan.  You
decide to stay close to the car.

[title33][sentence]
The balcony protrudes from the tackiest
condo in the history of modern architecture.
The white pillars make you wish you
had a chainsaw.  Francois would love
this place.
[title16][sentence]\nThe entrance is wide open.

[title27][sentence]
The vast cylindrical perimeter wall
stretches hundreds of feet over
your head.  At the top, you can see
a circle of bright blue sky.
[title25][sentence]\nThe city stretches off into the distance.

[title30][sentence]
As you stare at the statue, your
bladder begins to feel distinctly
smaller and tighter.  You quickly
force yourself to look away before
a horrible accident happens.

[title27][sentence]
The walls here look like they are
coated with something.  It's
probably some sort of sound
isolation.

[title26][sentence]
After being hit by that guard you
got to know the floor pretty well.
It doesn't hold your attention any
longer now than it did then.
[title25][sentence]\nThis corridor leads back to the cell block.
[title19][sentence]\nThere is a strange device part way down\nthis corridor.

[title28][sentence]
Judging by the size of the faucet there
must be a great deal of  cleaning up
to do around here.  You wonder what
sort of activity would require such
frequent large-scale cleaning.
[title18][sentence]\nThis looks like a normal sink.
[title20][sentence]\nThis must be where they put the\nless cooperative 'guests'.
[title21][sentence]\nThis large, sharp, intimidating blade\nsends a shiver down your spine.
[title13][sentence]\nThe monitor is not on.

[title26][sentence]
These are the strangest cabinets you
have ever seen.  They look more like
filing slots for loose limbs.  Your curiosity
regarding their contents quickly subsides.

[title24][sentence]
The equipment here is not unlike the
equipment in the rest of this complex.
Its purpose is completely beyond you.
[title25][sentence]\nThere are a few small red stains on the\nshelf.  It is otherwise uninteresting.
[title18][sentence]\nFor the moment, this is home.

[title25][sentence]
You are all too familiar with this
gurney.  You have no urge to lie
on it ever again.

[title27][sentence]
This must be where the attending 'physician'
keeps medical instruments.  The only items
of note on it are a corkscrew, a feather, and
a scalpel.  These do not look like 'friendly'
instruments.

[title27][sentence]
This is the small table you stole
the scalpel from.  There are not
any instruments on it just now.

[title27][sentence]
This must be some sort of examination room.
From your 'secure' position you see a large
saw blade, a pretty intern, and the ceiling.

[title30][sentence]
This is the medical examination room.
That pretty girl has left.  She must have finished
whatever she was doing with the instruments on the
table.
[title22][sentence]\nThis is the medical examination room.

[title25][sentence]
Sorry, they are locked and there
is no obvious locking mechanism
or insertion point for a key.
[title25][sentence]\nThis pretty young woman is tinkering\nwith something on the instrument table.

[title24][sentence]
The door is locked, barred, and probably
welded closed.  This is one woman you
won't be snooping on.  Besides, what if
she were actually in there?

[title25][sentence]
This woman is definitely 'well done'.  This
must be the professor the intern went to check
on after that explosion.  She has a tape recorder
in her hand.

[title27][sentence]
She appears to have quite a grip on
the tape recorder. There is an audio
tape inside it.

[title27][sentence]
This is the tape recorder you got
that little audio tape from.  She still
has a death-grip on it.

[title25][sentence]
You can't get the tape recorder loose from
her fingers.  She has a death-grip on it that
you just can't break.  You do manage to
open it and take out a small cassette.
[title26][sentence]\nThe professor's gurney is currently\nholding the charred professor off the floor.

[title32][sentence]
Quickly, while the intern is out of
the room, you reach out and grab the
scalpel.  You squirrel it away in your
sleeve and hope that no one will notice
its absence.

[title27][sentence]
You look up the elevator shaft.  You
can see that it does not stop at the upper
level of the city, but in fact runs all the
way up to the rim of the cylinder which the
city was built in.
[title29][sentence]\nThe elevator door is closed.  There is,\nhowever, a card slot adjacent to the left door.
[title25][sentence]\nIt appears that the elevator doesn't\nwork without some sort of access card.

[title29][sentence]
This culture must have taken their
designated handicapped parking spaces
seriously.  In fine print, at the bottom of
the sign, you read: "Violators will be given
good reason to park here."

[title26][sentence]
This looks like a hitching post for
horses.  The presence of such a device
strikes you as out of place in a city
which uses MLV's for transportation.

[title26][sentence]
Now THAT is a big mall.  There is
no end in sight.  There is no entrance
in sight, for that matter.  The mere thought
of entering a mall sends shivers down
your spine.

[title25][sentence]
Someone was running a special on
internal organs.  You wonder if they
were being sold as replacements, or as
stew meat.

[title25][sentence]
The street stretches off into the bowels
of the city.  You decide that it would be
best if you stayed close to the car.

[title29][sentence]
The street ends here.  You are at the edge
of the cylinder in which the city is built.
You are between a mall and an elevator.
[title25][sentence]\nIt's a safe bet that card slot adjacent to the left\ndoor operates the elevator.

[title29][sentence]
It won't fit.  Don't forget where you got
that security card.  It is no great surprise
that it's useless in this city.
[title22][sentence]\nIt hasn't changed while parked here.

[title29][sentence]
The brick continues up to the next level,
then gives way to sheet metal.  You pause
again to marvel at the size of the cylinder
in which this enormous city is built.

[title26][sentence]
The monitoring equipment looks like it
must have been used to keep tabs on
various automatic functions of the city.

[title25][sentence]
You are quite familiar with the Lemington OK-4
photon rifle.  It fires a coherent stream of
photons at the target, burning it to a crisp.
[title16][sentence]\nNot a chance.  The display case is impenetrable.

[title22][sentence]
The lovely display case holds a few
interesting weapons.  Unfortunately the
case is made of a material that is
truly Rex-proof.

[title32][sentence]
Cool!  You saw one of these on display
at a future weapons conference.  The
exhibition was phenomenal.  Ever since
then, you've always wanted to carry one
around in your back pocket.

[title26][sentence]
You are a bit thirsty, but the water
looks stagnant.  The bottle probably
hasn't been changed in at least a
hundred years.

[title27][sentence]
This large wooden box does not appear
to have any openings.  You would think
the top would lift off, but can't get it to
budge.
[title27][sentence]\nYou grunt and groan but accomplish nothing.\nThere must be some trick to it.

[title25][sentence]
You get an eerie feeling that maybe you 
shouldn't be here.  It's the same feeling
you had right before you were blown out
of the sky.

[title26][sentence]
You assume that this is where the booking process
takes place.  Reading you your rights, thumb
printing, taking mug shots . . . YOU know the routine.

[title25][sentence]
The monitor displays pertinent
information on suspects, such as hair
color, height, weight, social diseases, etc.
[title25][sentence]\nThis is an odd place for a filing cabinet.\nThey must have been moving it.
[title26][sentence]\nThe cabinets are empty.  They must have been\nmoving this just before they all went . . . where?

[title25][sentence]
The box contains a pair of odd-looking
objects that resemble detonators
for explosives.
[title13][sentence]\nThe box is now empty.
[title20][sentence]\nIt looks like someone left behind\na couple of detonators.

[title26][sentence]
You carefully pick up the detonators
and put them gingerly in your pocket, 
making a mental note not to do any
jumping jacks for a while.
[title18][sentence]\nYou see the edge of the city, and the\nsky above.

[title29][sentence]
The display case to the right contains
several interesting weapons.  There is
a guard station on the left, complete
with all manners of law enforcement
equipment.
[title25][sentence]\nYou would probably need a nuclear bomb \nto get this impenetrable case opened.

[title27][sentence]
It would most likely bounce off and possibly
bean you in the head.  Save your strength.

[title24][sentence]
A lone man seems the only inhabitant of
this grungy alley.  Several pairs of red
eyes watch you from dark hiding places.

[title25][sentence]
Since Herman has gone to his place in the woods,
only a few small rodents remain to scurry about
in the alley.

[title24][sentence]
The man in the alley seems extremely nervous
in your presence.  He looks as though he hasn't
taken a bath in a year or two.  You don't know
what the native life span is, but he looks ancient.
He is wearing some kind of personal stereo.
[title25][sentence]\nAll sorts of trash has been dumped here.\nThis looks like your bedroom on the Pig.
[title17][sentence]\nYou have absolutely no use for two thousand\npounds of miscellaneous trash.
[title21][sentence]\nThis could hold a large appliance for shipping\nor a mid-sized person for sleeping.
[title22][sentence]\nWhat are you going to do with that?\nTake it home and play in it?
[title25][sentence]\nIt has already been opened wide enough for you to realize\nthat it is empty.

[title21][sentence]
The refrigerator looks older that the
hermit.  Rust has replaced the enamel
finish in most places.  The hinges also
appear to be badly rusted.
[title19][sentence]\nNot likely.  Those hinges might as\nwell be welded solid.

[title25][sentence]
The last thing you need now is a hernia.
You don't normally go around trying
to stuff major appliances into your
pocket.  Why start now?

[title27][sentence]
The large buildings surrounding the
alley are weather worn and covered
with graffiti.

[title32][sentence]
For the most part, the graffiti on the wall
is no different from that which can be
found in any city on any world.  However,
a few random scribblings like "73766,347"
and "PTJT50A" strike you as unusual.
There are several good limericks and a
candid opinion about the questionable
parentage of someone named Bruce.  A
wave of poetic inspiration comes over
you, but after searching your pockets you
realize you forgot to bring your spray paint can.
